title: Quasi-coherent module descent on an algebraic-space groupoid
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Algebraic spaces and their small etale sites are [def-trf-algebraic-space]; quasi-coherent modules on them are [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and all pullbacks below are tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in algebraic spaces over $S$: its test-scheme points form groupoids, naturally in the test scheme, with source $s$, target $t$, identity $e$, inverse $i$, and composition $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ (first the second arrow, then the first). Let $\mathcal X=[U/R]$ be the fppf stackification of this presheaf of groupoids [lem-sfb-groupoid-stackification-local-description, def-pc-fppf-site]. Give $\mathcal X$ its big fppf site and structure sheaf [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]; quasi-coherence there means local presentation by small sums of $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$. Write $x:U\to\mathcal X$ for the canonical map. A groupoid module is a pair $(M,\alpha)$ with $M\in\operatorname{QCoh}(U)$ and an isomorphism $\alpha:t^*M\to s^*M$ such that $e^*\alpha=1$ and $c^*\alpha=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\alpha$ on $R\times_{s,U,t}R$, under the canonical pullback identifications. A morphism $(M,\alpha)\to(N,\beta)$ is a module map $v:M\to N$ with $s^*v\circ\alpha=\beta\circ t^*v$. Restriction $E:\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{QCoh}(U,R)$, given by $F\mapsto (x^*F|_{U_{\mathrm{et}}},\alpha_F)$ with the canonical comparison and groupoid two-isomorphism datum, is an equivalence of categories. No flatness or finiteness condition on $s,t,U,R$ is required.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal P=[U/_{p}R]$. Concretely an object is $(T,u)$ with $T$ an $S$-scheme and $u:T\to U$; an arrow $(f,r):(T,u)\to(T',u')$ has $f:T\to T'$, $r:T\to R$, $sr=u$, $tr=u'f$. The composite with $(g,r'):(T',u')\to(T'',u'')$ is $(gf,c(r'f,r))$, and the identity is $(1,e u)$. These are the category laws because the test-scheme points of the given groupoid are groupoids. A base map has the special cartesian lift $(f,e(u'f))$, and every arrow factors through such a lift followed by an invertible arrow over an identity. Thus $\mathcal P$ is fibred in groupoids, with no flatness assumption. Let $q:\mathcal P\to\mathcal X$ be stackification. Apply [lem-sfb-stackification-module-equivalence]: precomposition $q^*$ is an equivalence on quasi-coherent modules, with value $q^*F(T,u)=F(q(T,u))$. It suffices to construct the groupoid-module equivalence for $\mathcal P$. The functor $j:\underline U\to\mathcal P$ sends a test $u$ to $(T,u)$ and a base map to its special arrow; $qj=x$.

source.place: Tag 06WT, reduction to the prestack; Tag 06WR (lemma-stackification-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: For $H\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal P)$ set $M=H_j$, its small-etale restriction along $j$. By [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons], $M$ is quasi-coherent and all the comparison maps for arbitrary algebraic-space tests are isomorphisms, coherently with composition. The arrow $({\rm id},r):(T,sr)\to(T,tr)$ defines the universal two-isomorphism between $js$ and $jt$. Its contravariant comparison gives $\alpha:t^*M\to s^*M$. On a scheme test $r:T\to R$, this is the map on the small-etale modules induced by $H({\rm id},r)$, after the canonical comparison identifications. The identity arrow $(1,eu)$ gives $e^*\alpha=1$. On the composable test pair $(r'f,r)$ the identity $H((g,r')\circ(f,r))=H(f,r)\circ H(g,r')$, with the coherent pullback comparisons, gives $\alpha_{c(r'f,r)}=\alpha_r\circ f^*\alpha_{r'}$. Taking the universal composable pair gives precisely $c^*\alpha=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\alpha\circ\operatorname{pr}_0^*\alpha$. Naturality of comparisons in $H$ makes the restriction of any module map a compatible groupoid-module map. This defines a functor $E_{\mathcal P}$, and $E_{\mathcal P}q^*$ is the specified $E$, since $qj=x$ and the same universal arrows induce its two-isomorphism datum.

source.place: Tag 06WT, construction of the restriction functor; Tags 075D and 076R, comparison composition and two-isomorphisms

proof.text: Conversely take $(M,\alpha)$. For $y=(T,u)$ let $L_y$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski module corresponding to $u^*M$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Such a module exists by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent] and [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], with its specified natural comparison. For $(f,r):y\to y'$ define $\theta_{(f,r)}:f^*L_{y'}\to L_y$ by the etale-module isomorphism $$f^*(u')^*M\simeq (u'f)^*M=(tr)^*M\simeq r^*t^*M\xrightarrow{r^*\alpha}r^*s^*M\simeq u^*M.$$ Here [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] supplies the tensor composition identifications; the scheme etale/Zariski equivalence is compatible with every scheme pullback, so this determines the indicated Zariski module map. Every $\theta$ is an isomorphism because $\alpha$ is. All constructions are in the fixed size bound, and use arbitrary quasi-coherent modules, not finite-type modules.

source.place: Tag 06WT, inverse construction: modules on scheme tests; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03GA (lemma-pullback-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: For the identity of $(T,u)$, $r=eu$, so $\theta_{(1,eu)}=u^*e^*\alpha=1$. For $(f,r)$ followed by $(g,r')$, the cocycle pulled back along $(r'f,r):T\to R\times_{s,U,t}R$ says $$c(r'f,r)^*\alpha=r^*\alpha\circ f^*(r')^*\alpha.$$ Thus $\theta_{(gf,c(r'f,r))}=\theta_{(f,r)}\circ f^*\theta_{(g,r')}$. These equalities are between maps $(u''gf)^*M\to u^*M$. The canonical tensor comparisons introduce no extra automorphism: both parenthesizations send a local tensor $a\otimes(b\otimes(d\otimes m))$ to $a f^\sharp(b)(gf)^\sharp(d)\otimes m$, using the normalization in [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition]. To transport these equations to the Zariski modules $L_y$, use that the equivalence of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] is faithful: two Zariski maps $(gf)^*L_{y''}\to L_y$ agree once their etale images agree. By [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square] the comparison $\kappa_a:(a^*F)_{\mathrm{et}}\simeq a_{\mathrm{et}}^*F_{\mathrm{et}}$ is the mate, under the module adjunctions, of the identification $R_Ta_{\mathrm{et},*}\simeq a_*R_U$, the identity on open sections. The Zariski composition isomorphism $(gf)^*\simeq f^*g^*$ is the mate of $(gf)_*=g_*f_*$, and the tensor composition of [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] sends $1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to $1\otimes m$, so it is the mate of $(gf)_{\mathrm{et},*}=g_{\mathrm{et},*}f_{\mathrm{et},*}$. Since mates of composable squares compose, $\kappa_{gf}$ equals $f_{\mathrm{et}}^*\kappa_g\circ\kappa_f$ under these two composition isomorphisms; both are adjoint to the identity of $\Gamma((gf)^{-1}W,-)$ on an open $W\subseteq T''$. By naturality of $\kappa_f$, the etale image of $\theta_{(f,r)}\circ f^*\theta_{(g,r')}$ is the etale composite checked above, and the etale image of $\theta_{(gf,c(r'f,r))}$ is its etale map. Hence the cocycle holds for the $L_y$, and $\theta_{(1,eu)}=1$ because $\kappa_{\mathrm{id}}=1$.

source.place: Tag 06WT, omitted presheaf-functoriality verification, expanded using the stated cocycle

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-cartesian-module-fppf-realization] to $\mathcal P$, the $L_y$ and the $\theta$ just checked. It gives a quasi-coherent fppf module $B(M,\alpha)$ with $$B(M,\alpha)(T,u)=\Gamma(T,L_{(T,u)})=\Gamma(T,u^*M).$$ Restriction along $(f,r)$ pulls back a section along $f$ and then applies $r^*\alpha$. For a compatible map $v:(M,\alpha)\to(N,\beta)$, use $\Gamma(T,u^*v)$ on each object. The equality $s^*v\circ\alpha=\beta\circ t^*v$, pulled back along $r$, gives $u^*v\circ\theta^M_{(f,r)}=\theta^N_{(f,r)}\circ f^*(u')^*v$. Hence these section maps commute with all restrictions; they are module maps since pullback and $\alpha,\beta,v$ are module maps. Identities and composites are preserved objectwise. This defines the functor $B$ on objects and all morphisms. The realization theorem assumes neither that $U\to\mathcal X$ is an fppf morphism nor that $\mathcal X$ is algebraic.

source.place: Tag 06WT, section formula and the sheaf/quasi-coherence check; Tag 06WK (lemma-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: For every etale scheme chart $a:T\to U$, the small-etale restriction of $B(M,\alpha)$ along $(T,a)$ is $a^*M$: on an etale $b:T'\to T$ its sections are $\Gamma(T',(ab)^*M)$, and a special arrow has transition $1$ because $e^*\alpha=1$. The scheme etale/Zariski equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies this section sheaf with $a^*M$, naturally on the charts and their maps. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-cartesian-chart-family] these chart identifications give a natural isomorphism $E_{\mathcal P}B(M,\alpha)\simeq M$ on $U$. On a chart $r:T\to R$, the restriction along $({\rm id},r)$ in $B$ is exactly $\Gamma(T,r^*\alpha)$; restricting further to etale opens of $T$ proves equality of the module maps. Thus the isomorphism respects $\alpha$ on $R$, as required for a groupoid-module isomorphism. It is natural in $v$, since every component is $u^*v$ on charts.

source.place: Tag 06WT, omitted quasi-inverse verification, groupoid-module side; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03LY and 03LZ

proof.text: For the other composite start with $H\in\operatorname{QCoh}(\mathcal P)$ and $M=H_j$. For every $y=(T,u)$ the comparison of [lem-sfb-fibred-fppf-space-module-comparisons] gives $c_u:u^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}H_y$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$. Taking sections at $T$ gives $$\lambda_y:B(E_{\mathcal P}H)(T,u)=\Gamma(T,u^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(T,H_y)=H(T,u).$$ For a special arrow over $f$, composition compatibility of the $c_u$ says these maps commute with restriction. For an arrow $({\rm id},r)$ it says the same because $\alpha_r$ was defined from that arrow's comparison in step 2. Every $(f,r)$ factors as $({\rm id},r)$ followed by the special arrow over $f$, so the two verified squares give naturality for every arrow. Thus the $\lambda_y$ are an isomorphism of module sheaves $BE_{\mathcal P}H\simeq H$. Comparisons are natural in $H$, making this an isomorphism of functors. Together with step 6 it exhibits $B$ and $E_{\mathcal P}$ as quasi-inverses. Composing with the stackification equivalence of step 1 proves the specified $E$ is an equivalence. Every comparison used was for arbitrary maps between tests, so no flatness or finiteness assumption was introduced.

source.place: Tag 06WT, omitted quasi-inverse verification, sheaf side; Tag 06WR (lemma-stackification-quasi-coherent)
